title: Machine learning links a three-gene lung-cancer score to retrospective survival differences
summary: LASSO and random-forest selection identified a three-gene lung-adenocarcinoma score associated with observed survival in public cohorts. Comparison cohorts showed limited and inconsistent discrimination: TCGA five-year AUC was approximately 0.50, while another cohort reached approximately 0.68. This supports a bounded retrospective association, without established clinical utility or causal gene effects.
ai_technology: LASSO and random forests for prognostic gene selection; consensus clustering for RAS expression subtypes
organization: The Third People’s Hospital of Chengdu

evidence.tested: The source reports 624 GEO lung-adenocarcinoma profiles used for derivation. LASSO with ten-fold cross-validation and random-forest feature selection intersected at MAPK10, PLA2G12B and SHC3. The resulting score was compared with observed survival in TCGA and GSE13213. Reported one-, three- and five-year AUCs were 0.608, 0.535 and 0.496 in TCGA, and 0.620, 0.654 and 0.682 in GSE13213.
evidence.unknown: Outcome-optimized risk cutoffs limit interpretation of group survival differences as locked external prediction. Exact cohort eligibility accounting and supplementary implementation were not reconstructed. Weak TCGA discrimination limits clinical claims; decision-curve calculations do not demonstrate actual patient benefit. Transcriptomic associations and drug predictions do not establish causal mechanisms or treatment efficacy. Original online date is May 28, 2026; the assigned December issue is later.
evidence.ai_role: Learned LASSO and random-forest feature selection produced the three-gene signature whose relationship with measured patient survival was evaluated across cohorts. General clustering benchmarks and untested drug predictions are not the admitted finding.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary cohort acquisition, consensus clustering, gene selection, LASSO/random-forest and risk-score evaluation Methods, cohort survival/AUC Results and limitations. Supplementary code and individual-patient eligibility were not independently reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
